name: Compression
plain_language: Keep the parts that matter for the next decision and let go of the rest.
why_it_exists: Inputs, memories, images, and action histories are too large to carry forward unchanged.
everyday_setup: Compression starts from an ordinary constraint: Inputs, memories, images, and action histories are too large to carry forward unchanged. In the course atlas it appears in tokenization, embeddings, attention, latent space, where the same pressure shows up with different surface names.
formal_object: The formal object is the reusable handle that lets a model act on this pressure. For compression, that handle may be a vector, score, value estimate, probability, update rule, or state representation depending on the course.
symbol_explanation: `signal` means useful structure, `noise` means detail that does not help the next task, and `keep`/`discard` describe the representational choice.
course_appearances: In the transformer course, the primitive usually appears as a way to represent, route, or update context. In the RL course, it appears as a way to choose actions under delayed feedback. In the diffusion and vision course, it appears as a way to move through high-dimensional sample spaces.
misuse_failure: When compression is misused, the system optimizes the wrong handle: it may throw away needed detail, assign responsibility to the wrong source, trust unsupported futures, or report a score that hides the actual failure.
